table_title: For each continent, list the transboundary rivers in the cited Wikipedia source set that are at least 1000 kilometers long, including a boundary-aware continent label and the countries they traverse.
db_analog: SELECT continent_labels, river, length_km, countries FROM curated_transboundary_river_source_set WHERE length_km >= 1000 ORDER BY continent_labels, river
temporal_note: Wikipedia pages accessed in 2026. Core coverage comes from the Wikipedia "Transboundary river" page section "List of major international transboundary rivers", filtered to rows with length at least 1000 km. Additional omitted >=1000 km cross-country rivers were manually added from their dedicated Wikipedia pages for Africa, Asia, South America, and the Europe/Asia boundary, and Fly and Sepik were retained for Oceania. Expected cardinality for this curated Wikipedia source set is 33 rows.
_extraction_notes: Derived from the staged >100 miles version by raising the threshold to >=1000 km and then broadening the cited Wikipedia source set. Removed Ichamati (334), Meuse (925), Rhône (813), and St. Lawrence (500) because they fall below the new threshold. Retained all >=1000 km rows from Wikipedia's transboundary-river list, kept Fly and Sepik for Oceania, and added omitted >=1000 km cross-country rivers with dedicated Wikipedia pages: Senegal, Ubangi, Orange, Amur, Salween, Ili, Paraná, Paraguay, Uruguay, Madeira, and Ural. The schema now uses a boundary-aware `Continent(s)` field, so Ural is represented as `Europe; Asia` rather than being forced into a single continent bucket. This remains a curated Wikipedia-grounded set rather than an exhaustive global inventory.
